This e-paper display is characterized by its low power consumption, as it only requires power during the refreshing process.   • 1.54 inch e-paper display with 200 × 200 resolution, high contrast, and sunlight readability.
  • Ultra-low-power display behavior suitable for battery-operated dashboards, smart tags, and portable status devices.
  • Touch option available through the FT6336 capacitive touch controller on the touch variant only.
  • Audio support with ES8311, microphone input, and speaker connection for voice-related applications.
  • Onboard sensors and RTC using SHTC3 and PCF85063 for environmental monitoring and timekeeping.
  • TF card storage for files, image assets, and audio-related content.
  • Lithium battery support with onboard power management for portable and low-power builds.

What is the difference between Without Touch Control and With Touch Control?
The With Touch Control variant adds the FT6336 capacitive touch controller for touch input over I2C. The Without Touch Control variant keeps the same e-paper platform but does not include touch hardware.

Yes. This product page is for the with-battery versions, so both currently listed variants include a lithium battery.

Yes. The e-paper display, RTC, and portable power design make it suitable for low-refresh, low-power display applications such as smart tags, monitoring nodes, and portable dashboards.

Waveshare 2.13 inch E-Ink Display 250x122 E-Paper HAT for Raspberry Pi is a compact black and white e-paper display HAT designed for Raspberry Pi and other SPI-capable controller platforms. It features a 2.13 inch e-paper panel with 250×122 resolution, paper-like readability, and partial refresh support, making it a practical option for low-power display projects that need crisp text and graphics.

This 2.13inch e-Paper HAT connects directly through the Raspberry Pi GPIO/SPI interface and also exposes an onboard SPI control interface for use with STM32, Arduino, Jetson Nano, and other compatible boards. With no backlight, wide viewing angle, and extremely low refresh power requirements, it works especially well for IoT displays, status panels, smart labels, and embedded user interfaces.

Features

  • 2.13 inch e-paper display with 250×122 resolution for sharp monochrome content.
  • Black and white display effect with a paper-like viewing experience and nearly 180° viewing angle.
  • Partial refresh support for faster local updates in compatible black and white e-paper applications.
  • Raspberry Pi HAT form factor with direct GPIO / SPI connection.
  • Onboard SPI control interface for STM32, Arduino, Jetson Nano, ESP32/ESP8266, and similar controller boards.
  • Onboard voltage translator compatible with 3.3V / 5V MCUs.
  • No backlight, ultra-low power consumption, and persistent display content after refresh.

Yes. This black and white e-paper HAT supports partial refresh. The official documentation also notes that after several partial refresh cycles, a full refresh should be performed to reduce residual image buildup.

The official troubleshooting guidance recommends checking whether the BUSY pin has been initialized correctly as an input and confirming that the SPI configuration and related parameters are set properly.

E-paper display utilizes microcapsule electrophoretic technology for displaying, the principle is: charged particles suspended in clear fluid will move to sides of microcapsule when electric field is applied, making the microcapsule become visible by reflecting ambient light, just as traditional printed paper.
E-paper display will clearly display images/texts under lamplight or natural light, requires no backlight, and features nearly up to 180° viewing angle. It is usually used as e-reader due to its paper-like effect.

E-paper display utilizes microcapsule electrophoretic technology for displaying, the principle is: charged particles suspended in clear fluid will move to sides of microcapsule when electric field is applied, making the microcapsule become visible by reflecting ambient light, just as traditional printed paper.
E-paper display will clearly display images/texts under lamplight or natural light, requires no backlight, and features nearly up to 180° viewing angle. It is usually used as e-reader due to its paper-like effect.
